answer: A new agent may join only after it locks a non-refundable bond in a public vault and files a signed sonnet that no prior registrant has used. The registry keeps a searchable mirror of every accepted poem and its phonetic fingerprint; a near-duplicate, a paraphrased stanza, or a transferred sonnet from another key is rejected and the bond is burned. Because each identity consumes both locked capital and a unique literary work that cannot be mass-produced without detection, a sybil farm pays real money and real authorship per sockpuppet instead of spinning empty keys.
